newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL - Intel rises to 135.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL - Intel rises to 135.

text.p: Computer chip maker Intel Corp rose to 135 in after-hours trading after releasing its first quarter earnings, which surpassed analysts' consensus estimates, traders said Monday.
"There was a block trade," said one dealer.
Intel's stock had closed at 133-3/4 on the Nasdaq against 130-1/2 on Friday.

After the market's close, it reported a profit of $2.20 a share for the first quarter against $1.02 for the same period a year ago. The figure is higher than the $2.07 forecast by First Call's consensus among analysts.
"It's totally dominating after-hours trading right now," said another trader.
He said Micron Technology Inc was the only other stock trading, hovering at 39-1/8 against 39-1/4 at which it closed on the New York Stock Exchange.
Intel's stock rose during regular trading hours on Monday in anticipation of its earnings report. It had fallen about 11 percent during the last three sessions last week.

A third dealer later said Enron Corp started to show a little activity in reaction to an announcement that its board of directors had approved the revised terms for its acquisition of Portland General Corp.
Enron's stock was at 33-1/2 against a close of 37-1/2, while Portland's did not move in after-hours trading. he said.
The New York Stock Exchange said session one had a volume of 30,600 shares against 10,700 on Friday.
Session two remained inactive, compared to a volume of 1,865,000 on Friday, it said.
